subject: Compact per-route anomaly tile + adjustable sampling — request and constraints
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodelabs.com>
To: Observability Product <observability@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compact per-route anomaly tile + adjustable sampling — request and constraints

Hi team,

Quick ask from product — Acme's PM (cc'd on external thread below) asked for a compact console tile they can pin to show per-route cost and anomaly signal (spike % + tail latency percentile) with two constraints: it must be lightweight (no heavy tracebacks on load) and it needs an admin-configurable sampling knob per-tenant so they can enable higher fidelity only for VIP routes.

Goal: give customers a 1–2 row tile that summarizes: route name, 24h cost delta (USD), anomaly flag (green/amber/red), p95 latency, and a link to inspect (replay / traces) that is gated behind sampling.

Asks:
- Can engineering provide an implementation approach (approx. perf cost for dashboard queries) and a target SLO for tile load (<= 450ms on the page)?
- We need a sampling policy API (tenant + route + rate) and a UI toggle in Console for admins. Jasmine: can you mock the compact layout with an obvious affordance for "drill deeper"?
- Soojin/Naomi: we should define what qualifies as an "anomaly" for the tile (thresholds / algorithm). I'd like to avoid long-running anomaly jobs — prefer rolling-window heuristics.

Attachments: a quick spec (sampling_policy_spec.pdf) and an early mock (anomaly_tile_mock.png).

Timeline: Acme is asking for an early prototype by the end of Q3 (they want to pilot). For roadmap planning, can we flag technical blockers in replies?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

From: Eng Product (Acme) <eng-prod@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Observability follow-up

Jordan — we want a small dashboard widget that our Ops team can monitor without leaving the tenant home page. If sampling is needed to view traces, that's fine, but the tile should make it clear when sampling is on/off.

— Maya @ Acme

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodelabs.com>
Cc: Observability Product <observability@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact per-route anomaly tile + adjustable sampling — request and constraints

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the mock. A few clarifying items from infra/serving side: 

1) Tile query pattern: are we ok with a rollup query that reads pre-aggregated per-route metrics (cost delta, p95, p99) from the metrics store + a lightweight anomaly score computed on the last 24h window? If yes, we can avoid full trace scans.

2) Sampling API: implementing tenant+route sampling at the proxy layer is straightforward; the tricky bit is making sampling state visible in the UI and plumbed to downstream replay/traces + making sure sampled request stubs include a trace handle.

3) Perf budget: querying pre-aggregates and computing a simple z-score on a rolling window should be <200ms for the DB call in most regions, but UI render + network to backend for the inspect link could push to ~350–500ms on slower clients. We can probably meet <=450ms median but would need to cap payload size (no large inline traces).

Blockers/questions:
- Do we want the anomaly detection to run on write (streaming) vs on-read? Streaming adds infra complexity but gives faster, consistent anomaly flags.
- For sampling controls, do we want per-route defaults and tenant overrides? (I think yes).

I can spike the streaming vs on-read cost tomorrow and share numbers.

- Diego
Senior SWE, Serving

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact per-route anomaly tile + adjustable sampling — request and constraints

Love the compact direction. A couple UX notes after looking at the mock: 

- Keep the tile to a single line per-route for the default grid; expanding the tile should surface the last 3 anomalies with timestamps and a single-click "open in replay".
- The sampling toggle needs an explicit state: Disabled / Probabilistic (x%) / Full. Show inline indicator (small pill) and a tooltip that explains billing impact.
- For the inspect link, I suggest an intermediate "fast inspect" page that shows metadata + sampled-request timeline instead of immediately loading trace heavy components. This will satisfy the lightweight constraint.

I'll drop a Figma variant to the related_links (already uploaded). I can also add the tooltip copy and sample wording for the admin toggle.

— Jasmine
Product Designer, Console

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodelabs.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact per-route anomaly tile + adjustable sampling — request and constraints

Thanks, Diego + Jasmine — good notes. Quick responses: 

- Streaming vs on-read: for v1 let's do on-read heuristic (rolling 24h window z-score) to get the feature out fast and avoid infra changes. We can call out "eventual streaming" as a follow-up if customers want lower-latency flags.
- Sampling controls: yes, per-route defaults with tenant override. We should expose recommended defaults (0.1% for background, 2% for VIP routes) and let customers increase. Document billing implications in the tooltip (Jasmine to supply copy).
- Perf: if Diego can get a short spike with numbers for on-read compute plus DB read p95/p99, we can decide whether to gate the tile behind a caching layer (TTL 1m). If cache needed, product is fine with that.

Naomi: can you confirm any billing/quotas constraints we need to show on the Console before toggling sampling to higher rates?

I'll add OBS-1428 to our roadmap bucket as a dependency for the Acme pilot (they want an early prototype by EoQ3).

Jordan
